Definition: {to inquire; by implication, to request; by extension, to demand}
BiblicalUsage: Asking, in this Aramaic word, is usually demanding. The Chaldeans tell Nebuchadnezzar that no king has ever asked such a thing, and Daniel answers that the secret the king has demanded cannot be shown by any wise man. In Ezra the word turns official: the elders are asked who commanded the building, and Artaxerxes decrees that whatever Ezra requires shall be done.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the point is the contrast: earthly kings demand answers no man can give, and God gives them freely to the one who asks Him. Daniel could answer only because the God of heaven had shown him the secret.
